craft_claim: Sustained audience absorption relies on an overarching dominant aesthetic emotion (sthayi bhava / rasa) into which transient emotional states resolve.

supporting_evidence.note: Bharata explains that no meaning can proceed without rasa: the combination of vibhava, anubhava, and vyabhicaribhava produces emotional relish.
Anandavardhana establishes that rasa-dhvani (suggested emotion) represents the highest tier of poetic resonance.
The entire drama is unified by Sringara rasa, where transient fear, anger, and grief are resolved into transcendent aesthetic love.

scope: Applies across Indian dramatic poetics and global dramatic and narrative emotional design.
exceptions: Brechtian epic theatre or alienation aesthetics designed to actively disrupt emotional absorption.
